paragraphs: Ventas, Inc. is an S&P 500 company focused on delivering strong, sustainable shareholder returns by enabling exceptional environments that benefit a large and growing aging population. We hold a portfolio that includes senior housing communities, outpatient medical buildings, research centers, hospitals and healthcare facilities located in North America and the United Kingdom. As of December 31, 2025, we owned or had investments in 1,409 properties consisting of 1,374 properties in our reportable segments ("Segment Properties") and 35 properties held by unconsolidated real estate entities in our non-segment operations. We are headquartered in Chicago, Illinois with additional corporate offices in Louisville, Kentucky and New York, New York.

We elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") under Sections 856 through 860 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"), commencing with our taxable year ended December 31, 1999. Provided we qualify for taxation as a REIT, we generally are not required to pay U.S. federal corporate income taxes on our REIT taxable income that is currently distributed to our stockholders. In order to maintain our qualification as a REIT, we must satisfy a number of technical requirements, which impact how we invest in, operate and manage our assets. See "Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our REIT Status" included in Part I, Item 1A of this Annual Report.

We operate through three reportable segments: senior housing operating portfolio, which we refer to as "SHOP," outpatient medical and research portfolio, which we refer to as "OM&R," and triple-net leased properties, which we refer to as "NNN." We also hold assets outside of our reportable segments, which we refer to as non-segment assets, and which consist primarily of corporate assets, including cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, loans receivable and investments, accounts receivable and investments in unconsolidated entities. Our investments in unconsolidated entities include investments made through our third-party institutional private capital management platform, Ventas Investment Management ("VIM"). Through VIM, we partner with third-party institutional investors to invest in real estate through various joint ventures and other co-investment vehicles where we are the sponsor or general partner, including our open-ended investment vehicle, the Ventas Life Science & Healthcare Real Estate Fund (the "Ventas Fund"). Our investments in unconsolidated entities also include investments in operating entities, such as Ardent Health, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, "Ardent") and Atria Senior Living, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, "Atria"). See our Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes, including "Note 7 – Investments in Unconsolidated Entities" included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report.

Our chief operating decision maker evaluates performance of the combined properties in each operating segment and determines how to allocate resources to these segments based on net operating income ("NOI") for each segment. See our Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes, including "Note 2 – Accounting Policies" and "Note 18 – Segment Information" included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report.

(1) "NOI" is defined as total revenues, less interest and other income, property-level operating expenses and third-party capital management expenses. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" included elsewhere in this Annual Report for additional disclosure and a reconciliation of Net income attributable to common stockholders, as computed in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"), to NOI.

(2) NOI for non-segment includes management fees and promote revenues, net of expenses related to our third-party institutional private capital management platform, income from loans and investments and corporate-level expenses not directly attributable to any of our three reportable segments.

For nearly three decades, Ventas has pursued a strategy focused on delivering outsized value to stockholders and other key stakeholders by enabling exceptional environments that benefit a large and growing aging population. Working with industry-leading care providers, partners and research and medical institutions, our collaborative and experienced team is focused on achieving consistent, superior total returns through: (1) delivering profitable organic growth in senior housing, (2) capturing value-creating external growth focused on senior housing, (3) generating strong cash flow throughout our portfolio of high-quality assets unified in meeting demographic demand and (4) maintaining financial strength, flexibility and liquidity.

Our objective is to generate reliable and growing cash flows from our portfolio, which enables us to pay regular cash dividends to stockholders and creates opportunities to increase stockholder value.

In our SHOP segment, we own and invest in senior housing communities. We participate directly in the financial performance of the communities' operations and are generally responsible for all operational costs, expenses and other liabilities. We typically engage third-party managers to operate the communities on our behalf but generally hold applicable healthcare licenses and enroll in applicable government healthcare programs on behalf of the communities in our SHOP segment.

In order to support our SHOP segment, we developed Ventas OI™, a proprietary data and analytics platform, to provide us with timely access to high-quality data that informs real-time decisions. Through Ventas OI™, we collect and assess data from a variety of sources, including proprietary data from our senior housing operations and external data sources. This data supports business models and automated dashboard reporting that are enabled by machine learning, providing us with reporting systems & business intelligence dashboards, marketing and sales analytics, competitive intelligence and geospatial analytics. Ventas OI™ blends our operational expertise and data analytics to engage the managers, enhance the performance of our communities and elevate the quality of care and services delivered to residents. We also leverage Ventas OI™ for our investment and capital expenditure decisions.

The senior housing communities in our SHOP segment include independent living communities, assisted living communities, memory care communities and continuing care retirement communities. Independent living communities are typically age-restricted multifamily rental properties with central dining facilities that provide residents with access to meals and other services such as housekeeping, linen service, transportation and social and recreational activities. Assisted living communities typically offer similar services as independent living communities, plus supportive care that is provided by trained employees to residents who require assistance with activities of daily living, such as bathing, dressing and medication management. Memory care communities provide care for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia or memory loss. Continuing care retirement communities are typically age-restricted properties that offer a continuum of care, and may include a combination of independent living, assisted living, memory care and skilled nursing units. Our assisted living, memory care and continuing care retirement communities are generally subject to state licensure requirements for the delivery of some or all of their services, while our independent living communities generally are not. Charges for room, board and services at these communities are generally paid from private sources, with limited reliance on government reimbursement programs such as Medicaid.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business Operations and Strategy
Macroeconomic trends, including trends relating to labor costs, unemployment, inflation, interest rates and exchange rates, may affect our business and financial results.

Changes in the U.S. political and regulatory environment could affect availability of government funding that we or our managers, tenants or borrowers rely on, which could negatively impact our business.

To the extent that we or our managers, tenants and borrowers are unable to navigate successfully the trends affecting our or their businesses and the industries in which we or they operate, we may be adversely affected.
Our managers and tenants operate or exert substantial control over the properties that they manage or lease from us, which limits our control and influence over operations and results.
If our managers', tenants' or borrowers' financial condition or business prospects deteriorate, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.
We face potential adverse consequences from the bankruptcy or insolvency of our managers, tenants, borrowers and other obligors.
A significant portion of our revenues and operating income is dependent on a limited number of tenants and managers, including Ardent, Kindred, Atria, Sunrise and Le Groupe Maurice.
We are vulnerable to adverse changes affecting our specific asset classes and the real estate industry generally.
Ownership of properties or operation of our business outside the United States may subject us to different or greater risks than those associated with our domestic operations.
The hospitals on or near the campuses where our outpatient medical buildings are located and their affiliated health systems may not remain competitive or financially viable.
Our research tenants face unique levels of expense and uncertainty.

If a borrower defaults, we may be unable to obtain payment, successfully foreclose on collateral or realize the value of any collateral, which could adversely affect our ability to recover our investment.
Our ongoing strategy depends, in part, upon identifying and consummating future acquisitions and investments and effectively managing our external growth opportunities.
Our investments and acquisitions may be unsuccessful or fail to meet our expectations.
Our investments in co-investment vehicles, joint ventures and minority interests may subject us to risks that we would not otherwise face.
Increased construction and development in the markets in which our properties are located could adversely affect our future occupancy rates, operating margins and profitability.
Development, redevelopment and construction risks could affect our profitability.
Damage from catastrophic or extreme weather or other natural events could result in losses to the Company.
We may be unable to sell certain properties on a timely basis or on favorable terms, which may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
paragraphs: This section discusses material factors that affect our business, operations and financial condition. It does not describe all risks and uncertainties applicable to us, our industry or ownership of our securities. If any of the following risks, or any other risks and uncertainties that are not addressed below or that we have not yet identified, actually occur, we could be materially adversely affected, and the value of our securities could decline.
As set forth below, we believe that the risks we face generally fall into the following categories:
•Risks Relating to Our Business Operations and Strategy •Risks Relating to Our Capital Structure
•Risks Relating to Legal, Compliance and Regulatory •Risks Relating to Our REIT Status

Macroeconomic trends, including unfavorable trends relating to labor costs, unemployment, inflation, interest rates and exchange rates, may adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Increased labor costs and a shortage of available skilled and unskilled workers may impact our or our managers', tenants' or borrowers' workforce, including employees at our senior housing communities. To the extent we or our managers, tenants or borrowers cannot hire sufficient qualified workers, we or they may need to rely on high-cost alternatives to meet labor needs, including contract and overtime labor. In addition, we and our managers, tenants and borrowers compete with various other companies in attracting and retaining qualified and skilled personnel. Competitive pressures may require that we or our managers, tenants or borrowers enhance pay and benefits packages to compete effectively for such personnel. We and our managers, tenants and borrowers may not be able to offset additional staffing costs by increasing the rates we charge, whether to residents, tenants or others. If there is an increase in these costs or if we or our managers, tenants and borrowers fail to attract and retain qualified and skilled personnel, our respective businesses and operating results could be adversely affected. See also "—To the extent that we or our managers, tenants and borrowers are unable to navigate successfully the trends affecting our or their businesses and the industries in which we or they operate, we may be adversely affected."

paragraphs: Ventas, Inc. 為一間上市於 S&P 500 的公司，專注於透過提供優良且可持續的投資回報，來營造對廣大且持續成長的年長人口有益的環境。我們的資產組合包含高齡住宅社區、門診醫療大樓、研究中心、醫院及醫療設施，位於北美與英國。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有或投資於 1,409 項不動產，其中 1,374 項為應報告分部（"Segment Properties"），另外 35 項為未合併不動產實體所持有，屬於我們的非應報告分部。我們的總部設於美國伊利諾州芝加哥，並在肯塔基州路易維爾與紐約州紐約設有其他營運辦公室。

我們已選擇以不動產投資信託（"REIT"）方式納稅，根據 1986 年美國內政部稅法（"Code"）第 856 至 860 節，自 1999 年度財稅年度開始。只要我們符合 REIT 的納稅資格，我們通常不需要就分派給股東的 REIT 稅收所得支付美國聯邦公司所得稅。為維持我們的 REIT 資格，我們必須符合多項技術性要求，這些要求影響我們對資產的投資、營運與管理方式。請參閱本年度報告第一部分第 1A 項所包含的 "風險因素—與我們 REIT 資格相關的風險"。

我們透過三個應報告分部進行營運：高齡住宅營運資產組合，我們稱為 "SHOP"；門診醫療與研究資產組合，我們稱為 "OM&R"；以及三重淨租賃不動產，我們稱為 "NNN"。我們也持有非應報告分部的資產，我們稱為非應報告資產，主要為公司資產，包括現金與現金等價物、受限現金、應收貸款、投資、應收款與對未合併實體的投資。我們對未合併實體的投資包括透過我們第三方機構私人資本管理平台 Ventas Investment Management（"VIM"）所進行的投資。透過 VIM，我們與第三方機構投資者合作，透過各種合資企業及其他共同投資工具進行不動產投資，我們為發起人或普通合夥人，包括我們的開放式投資工具，Ventas Life Science & Healthcare Real Estate Fund（"Ventas Fund"）。我們對未合併實體的投資也包括對營運實體的投資，例如 Ardent Health, Inc.（連同其子公司，"Ardent"）與 Atria Senior Living, Inc.（連同其子公司，"Atria"）。請參閱我們的合併財務報表與相關附註，包括 "第 7 註—對未合併實體的投資"，包含於本年度報告第二部分第 8 項。
我們的最高經營決策者評估每個營運分部的整體不動產表現，並根據每個分部的淨營運收入（"NOI"）來決定如何分配資源至這些分部。請參閱我們的合併財務報表與相關附註，包括 "第 2 註—會計政策" 以及 "第 18 註—分部資訊"，包含於本年度報告第二部分第 8 項。
下表總結了我們資產組合於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度的資訊（單位為千美元）：
高齡住宅營運資產組合（SHOP） $ 1,184,064 49.4 % 752 門診醫療與研究資產組合（OM&R） 590,169 24.7 % 409
(1) "NOI" 定義為總收入，扣除利息及其他收入、不動產層級營運費用與第三方資本管理費用。請參閱本年度報告其他部分所包含的 "非 GAAP 財務指標"，以取得更多揭露資訊，並說明根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）計算的歸屬於普通股股東的淨收入與 NOI 之間的關係。
（2）非應報告分部的 NOI 包含管理費及促銷收入，扣除與我們第三方機構私人資本管理平台相關的費用，貸款及投資收入，以及與我們三個應報告分部無直接關聯的公司層級費用。

近三十年來，Ventas 一直致力於透過創造對大眾年長人口有益的優質環境，為股東及其他關鍵利害關係人帶來超額價值。與行業領先的照護機構、合作夥伴及研究與醫療機構合作，我們經驗豐富且具備團隊精神的團隊，專注於透過以下方式實現穩定且優越的總回報：（1）在長者住宅領域實現獲利的內生成長，（2）透過長者住宅領域實現創造價值的外生成長，（3）透過我們高品質資產組合產生強勁現金流，這些資產組合符合人口結構需求，（4）維持財務強韌性、靈活性與流動性。
我們的目標是透過我們的資產組合產生穩定且成長的現金流，這使我們能夠向股東支付定期現金股息，並創造增加股東價值的機會。
在我們的 SHOP 分部，我們擁有並投資長者住宅社區。我們直接參與社區營運的財務表現，並通常承擔所有營運成本、費用及其他負債。我們通常委託第三方經理人代表我們營運社區，但通常會為社區持有適用的醫療許可證，並為社區 enrol 在適用的政府醫療保險計畫中。

為支援我們的 SHOP 分部，我們開發了 Ventas OI™，這是一個專屬的數據與分析平台，以提供我們即時取得高品質數據的管道，這些數據可用於做出即時決策。透過 Ventas OI™，我們從多種來源收集並評估數據，包括來自我們長者住宅營運的專屬數據與外部數據來源。這些數據支持由機器學習驅動的商業模式與自動化儀錶板報告，提供我們報表系統與商業智慧儀錶板、行銷與銷售分析、競爭情報與地理空間分析。Ventas OI™ 結合我們的營運專業知識與數據分析，以與經理人合作，提升我們社區的表現，並提高對居民提供的照護與服務品質。我們也利用 Ventas OI™ 進行投資與資本支出決策。

我們 SHOP 分部的長者住宅社區包括獨立生活社區、輔助生活社區、記憶照護社區與持續照護退休社區。獨立生活社區通常是年齡限制的多戶出租住宅，設有中央餐飲設施，為居民提供餐點及其他服務，例如清潔、牀單服務、交通與社交與休閒活動。輔助生活社區通常提供與獨立生活社區類似的服務，並提供由訓練員工提供的支持性照護，以協助需要協助日常活動的居民，例如洗澡、穿衣與藥物管理。記憶照護社區為患有阿爾茨海默症及其他形式失智或記憶喪失的個別提供照護。持續照護退休社區通常是年齡限制的住宅，提供連續的照護，可能包含獨立生活、輔助生活、記憶照護與專業護理單位的組合。我們的輔助生活、記憶照護與持續照護退休社區通常需符合各州對部分或全部服務的執照要求，而我們的獨立生活社區通常無此要求。這些社區的房間、膳食與服務費用通常由私人來源支付，政府補助計畫如醫療救助的依賴程度有限。

paragraphs: 以下討論提供管理階層認為與瞭解及評估 Ventas, Inc. 組合財務狀況及營運成果相關之資訊。您應配合本公司合併財務報表及相關附註，並參閱本年度報告第二部分，第 8 項「合併財務報表」及第一部分，第 1A 項「風險因素」之內容閱讀本討論。

Ventas, Inc.（含其合併子公司，除非另有說明或語境另有要求，否則均指「我們」、「我們」、「我們」、「Ventas」、「公司」及其他類似詞彙）為 S&P 500 公司，專注於透過創造優良環境，使龐大且持續成長的老年人口受益，以實現強勁且可持續的股東回報。我們持有包含長照社區、門診醫療大樓、研究中心、醫院及醫療設施之資產組合，這些資產位於北美及英國。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有或投資於 1,409 處不動產，其中 1,374 處為應報告分部（「分部不動產」），35 處為未合併不動產實體所持有，屬於我們非分部營運。我們總部設於美國伊利諾州芝加哥，並在肯塔基州路易維爾及紐約州紐約設有其他營運辦公室。

我們已選擇根據 1986 年美國聯邦稅法（Code）第 856 至 860 節，以不動產投資信託（REIT）方式課稅，自 1999 年財稅年度（截至 1999 年 12 月 31 日）開始。只要我們符合 REIT 的課稅資格，我們通常無需就目前分派給股東之 REIT 稅收所得支付美國聯邦公司所得稅。為維持我們作為 REIT 的資格，我們必須符合若干技術性要求，這些要求影響我們對資產的投資、營運及管理方式。請參閱本年度報告第一部分，第 1A 項「風險因素—與我們 REIT 狀態相關的風險」。

我們透過三個應報告分部營運：長照社區營運資產組合（我們稱為「SHOP」）、門診醫療及研究資產組合（我們稱為「OM&R」），以及三重淨租賃不動產（我們稱為「NNN」）。我們也持有非應報告分部資產（我們稱為「非分部資產」），主要為公司資產，包括現金及現金等價物、限制性現金、應收貸款、投資、應收款及對未合併實體之投資。我們對未合併實體之投資包括透過我們第三方機構私人資本管理平台 Ventas Investment Management（「VIM」）所進行之投資。透過 VIM，我們與第三方機構投資者合作，透過各種合資企業及其他共同投資工具進行不動產投資，我們為發起人或普通合夥人，包括我們的開放式投資工具 Ventas Life Science & Healthcare Real Estate Fund（「Ventas 基金」）。我們對未合併實體之投資也包括對營運實體之投資，例如 Ardent Health, Inc.（含其子公司，「Ardent」）及 Atria Senior Living, Inc.（含其子公司，「Atria」）。請參閱我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，包括第二部分，第 8 項「附註 7—對未合併實體之投資」。
我們的最高經營決策者評估各營運分部合併不動產之表現，並根據各分部之淨營運收入（NOI）決定如何分配資源至這些分部。請參閱我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，包括第二部分，第 8 項「附註 2—會計政策」及「附註 18—分部資訊」。
以下表格總結我們於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年終之資產組合資訊（金額單位為千美元）：
長照社區營運資產組合（SHOP） $ 1,184,064 49.4 % 752 門診醫療及研究資產組合（OM&R） 590,169 24.7 % 409
(1) "NOI" 為總營業收入，減去利息及其它收入、物業層營運費用及第三方資本管理費用。請參閱本年度報告其他部分所包含的 "Non-GAAP 財務指標" 項目，以取得更多揭露資訊及將根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）計算的歸屬於普通股股東的淨收入，與 NOI 的對應關係說明。
(2) 非應報告分部的 NOI 包含管理費及促銷收入，扣除與我們第三方機構私人資本管理平台相關的費用，以及貸款及投資收入，以及與我們三個應報告分部無直接關係的公司層費用。

近三十年來，Ventas 一直致力於透過建立優秀的環境，以提供給龐大且持續成長的老年人口帶來利益，來為股東及其他關鍵利害關係人創造超額價值。與行業領先的照護機構、合作夥伴及研究與醫療機構合作，我們具備經驗的團隊專注於透過以下方式實現穩定且優異的總回報：(1) 在長者住宅領域實現獲利的內生成長，(2) 抓取針對長者住宅的價值創造外在成長，(3) 透過我們高品質資產組合產生強勁現金流，這些資產組合統合以應對人口結構需求，以及 (4) 保持財務強韌性、靈活性與流動性。
我們的目標是從我們的資產組閤中產生穩定且成長的現金流，這使我們能夠向股東支付定期現金股息，並創造增加股東價值的機會。
我們預期長者住宅將受益於強勁的供需基本面，包括強勁的預測需求成長與低預測供給成長。長者住宅預期將受益於美國龐大且持續成長的老年人口，80 歲以上人口預計到 2030 年將成長 28%。美國長者住宅的建設開工數量目前處於歷史低點。
我們的營運已受到並預期將持續受到更廣泛經濟與市場條件的影響，包括利率、通貨膨脹以及資本與勞動市場的狀況。

headings: 與我們業務運作及策略相關的風險
總體經濟趨勢，包括與勞動成本、失業率、通貨膨脹、利率及匯率相關的趨勢，可能影響我們的業務與財務結果。
美國政治與法規環境的變化可能影響我們或我們的經理人、租戶或貸款人所依賴的政府資金可得性，這可能會對我們的業務產生負面影響。
若我們或我們的經理人、租戶及貸款人無法成功應對影響我們或他們的業務及其所從事產業的趨勢，我們可能會受到不利影響。
我們的經理人及租戶運作或對其管理或租賃的不動產擁有相當程度的控制權，這會限制我們對運作及結果的控制與影響力。
若我們的經理人、租戶或貸款人的財務狀況或業務前景惡化，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
我們可能因經理人、租戶、貸款人及其他義務人的破產或財務困難而面臨潛在的負面後果。
我們收入及營運收入的相當大一部分取決於為數不多的租戶及經理人，包括 Aardent、Kindred、Atria、Sunrise 及 Le Groupe Maurice。
我們易受影響於不利變動，這些變動可能影響我們特定資產類別以及整體不動產業務。
我們在美國境外擁有不動產或經營業務，可能會使我們面臨與美國境內業務不同的風險，或風險程度更高。
我們 outpatient 醫療大樓所在地的醫院及其相關醫療系統，可能無法維持競爭力或財務可行性。
我們的研究租戶面臨獨特的費用與不確定性層次。
若借款人違約，我們可能無法取得償還、成功實現擔保品或實現擔保品價值，這可能會對我們回收投資的能力造成不利影響。
我們持續的策略部分依賴於識別並完成未來的收購與投資，並有效管理我們的外部成長機會。
我們的投資與收購可能無法成功，或未能達到我們的預期。
我們在共同投資工具、合資企業及少數股權上的投資，可能使我們面臨我們通常不會遇到的風險。
本公司所處市場之建物建設與開發活動增加，可能對未來租賃率、營運毛利及利潤產生負面影響。
開發、重建及建設風險可能影響本公司之利潤。
因災難性或極端天氣或其他自然事件所致之損壞，可能導致本公司產生損失。
本公司可能無法及時或以有利條件出售特定不動產，此情形可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
paragraphs: 本節討論影響本公司業務、營運及財務狀況的重大因素。並未說明所有適用於本公司、我們產業或本公司證券持有者的風險與不確定性。若任何下列風險，或任何未於下文提及或其他尚未識別的風險與不確定性實際發生，本公司可能遭受重大不利影響，且本公司證券的價值可能下跌。
如下列所載，我們認為我們所面臨的風險大致可歸納為以下類別：
•與本公司業務營運與策略相關的風險 •與本公司資本結構相關的風險
•與法律、合規與監管相關的風險 •與本公司REIT地位相關的風險
總體經濟趨勢，包括與勞動成本、失業率、通貨膨脹、利率及匯率相關的不利趨勢，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。

勞動成本增加及可用技術與非技術勞工短缺可能影響本公司或本公司管理機構、租戶或借款人的員工，包括我們高齡住宅社區的員工。若本公司或本公司管理機構、租戶或借款人在無法聘僱足夠合格員工的情況下，可能需要依賴高成本替代方案以滿足勞動需求，包括合約與 overtime 勞動。此外，本公司與本公司管理機構、租戶及借款人在吸引與留住合格且具專業技能人員方面，與其他公司競爭。競爭壓力可能要求本公司或本公司管理機構、租戶或借款人提升薪資與福利方案，以有效競爭這些人才。本公司與本公司管理機構、租戶及借款人可能無法透過提高對居民、租戶或其他人收取的費用來抵消額外的人事成本。若這些成本增加，或本公司或本公司管理機構、租戶及借款人無法吸引與留住合格且具專業技能人員，則我們的業務與營運成果可能受到負面影響。另請參閱 "—若本公司或本公司管理機構、租戶及借款人無法成功應對影響我們或其業務與所從事產業的趨勢，本公司可能受到負面影響。"
